name: Grace-Meridian
geological_features: Frozen mineral springs that thaw seasonally
Layered sedimentary cliffs revealing eons of geological history
description: Grace-Meridian is a small terrestrial world where thin atmosphere and low gravity have conspired to create landscapes of impossible delicacy. Sandstone arches span kilometers without support, their forms carved by patient winds into shapes that seem to defy structural logic, curving and branching like the limbs of dancers frozen mid-performance.

The thin air carries sound poorly but light beautifully, painting the sky in gradient washes of amber and violet that shift with the planet's slow rotation. There is an elegance to this world that feels intentional, as though some cosmic sculptor shaped it with deliberate aesthetic purpose.

Microbial life thrives in the seasonal mineral springs, erupting in brilliant chromatic blooms when the frozen aquifers thaw during the planet's perihelion approach. These organisms have evolved pigmentation so vivid that their colonies are visible from orbit, painting the cliff faces in streaks of crimson and gold.

Grace-Meridian has no strategic value and little in the way of exploitable resources, yet it draws visitors from across the sector who come simply to witness its beauty. Proposals to establish an artists' colony here have gained traction, though purists argue that any permanent settlement would diminish the very quality that makes the world remarkable.
